extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for ICLR 2025 Area Chairs on writing meta-reviews and making accept/reject decisions, including required meta-review structure, decision criteria, and calibration procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review minimum length
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs should write meta-reviews of at least 60 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document explicitly requires meta-reviews to be a minimum of 60 words to ensure sufficient detail; use that space to include the three key elements (content summary, discussion summary, recommendation with justification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise description of the submission's main content (scientific claims and findings) including strengths, weaknesses, and what's missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the paper's core claims and results, list primary strengths and weaknesses, and note substantive gaps or missing experiments/analyses. This should be succinct but informative for program chairs and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesize weeks of reviewer–author dialogue, listing points raised by reviewers, how authors addressed them, and the AC's assessment of their merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear synthesis of review threads: enumerate major reviewer concerns, summarize the authors' responses and revisions, and evaluate whether those responses adequately resolved the concerns. Treat reviewer arguments and author rebuttals explicitly so chairs can see how issues were handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation with Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The meta-review must conclude with a clear accept/reject recommendation grounded in the paper's content and discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give an explicit final decision (accept or reject) and justify it by tying back to the content summary and the discussion summary—do not leave the recommendation ambiguous. The justification should explain why remaining issues (if any) do or do not warrant rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base decisions on paper quality (not score curves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Base recommendations for accept/reject based solely on the reviews and the quality of papers (not score curves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize intrinsic manuscript quality—technical soundness, novelty, empirical support—over numerical acceptance-rate targets or score distributions. Avoid using acceptance quotas or curve-fitting as a basis for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with ICLR 2025 reviewer guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations should be aligned with ICLR 2025 reviewer guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that assessments and final recommendations reflect the criteria and standards laid out in the official reviewer guidance (e.g., significance, validity, clarity, reproducibility) so decisions are consistent with conference policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Ethics compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider compliance with the Code of Ethics when forming recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for ethical issues (e.g., plagiarism, harmful content, conflicts of interest) and factor any violations or concerns into the recommendation and justification. Explicitly mention ethical concerns in the meta-review if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use virtual meeting discussions for borderline papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtual meeting discussions should be used to resolve borderline cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper is on the borderline after reviews and author responses, escalate it to the program's virtual discussion/meeting process for further deliberation before finalizing the meta-review recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek calibration support when uncertain
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs should contact their Senior Area Chair or program chairs if uncertain about recommendations, ensuring decisions reflect paper quality rather than predetermined acceptance quotas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt about how to interpret reviews, the adequacy of author responses, or where a paper stands relative to program standards, proactively consult SACs or PCs for calibration advice rather than unilaterally adjusting standards to meet perceived quotas.
